reforms.description: The Japanese government provided financial assistance through grants, concessional loans, and tax benefits to promote the development of technologically-advanced industries, including industrial machinery and information electronics.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: The financial assistance is aimed at fostering innovation and technological development, which can enhance productivity and economic growth.
reforms.status_evidence: The reform has been actively providing financial assistance as stated.
reforms.importance_rationale: The reform represents a significant policy change aimed at supporting advanced industries, indicating its major importance.
reforms.source_quote: The expansion of technologically-sophisticated industries was promoted by specific development plans formulated by MITI and government financial assistance provided under various schemes.
reforms.cross_verification_note: The description mentions 'financial assistance through grants, concessional loans, and tax benefits' to promote 'the development of technologically-advanced industries', which aligns with direct public R&D funding.

reforms.description: Japan launched the 'Sunshine project' in 1974 to promote technological research and development for new energy sources, involving participation of the Government and the Japan Development Bank.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Directed R&D in new energy sources addresses long-term energy security and technological capability, supporting productivity and innovation.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant sectoral R&D initiative with government and development bank participation, but narrower in scope than economy-wide industrial policy.
reforms.source_quote: The 'Sunshine project' aiming at promoting technological research and development for new energy sources was started in 1974 involving the participation of the Government and that of the Japan Development Bank.
reforms.cross_verification_note: The 'Sunshine project' is explicitly aimed at 'promoting technological research and development for new energy sources', which qualifies as sectoral R&D.

reforms.description: Japan launched the 'Moonlight project' in 1978 to promote research and development for energy conservation across industrial sectors.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Directed R&D in energy conservation technology supports productivity improvements and resource efficiency across industrial sectors.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant sectoral R&D initiative addressing energy conservation across multiple industries, but narrower than economy-wide policy.
reforms.source_quote: In 1978 a new 'Moonlight project' was launched to promote research and development for energy conservation.
reforms.cross_verification_note: The 'Moonlight project' is focused on 'promoting research and development for energy conservation', which falls under sectoral R&D.

reforms.description: Japan implemented specific development plans formulated by MITI to promote technologically-advanced industries (industrial machinery, information electronics, aircraft, nuclear energy) through government financial assistance including grants, concessional loans, special tax benefits for R&D projects, and joint ventures to promote domestic technology development.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Targeted R&D funding and tax incentives for technologically-advanced sectors directly support innovation, productivity, and industrial competitiveness.
reforms.importance_rationale: Structural, system-wide industrial policy coordinating multiple funding instruments (grants, loans, tax benefits, joint ventures) across multiple strategic sectors.
reforms.source_quote: The expansion of technologically-sophisticated industries was promoted by specific development plans formulated by MITI and government financial assistance provided under various schemes. This has essentially taken the form of grants, concessional loans and special tax benefits for research and development projects, as well as joint ventures to promote the development of domestic technology.
reforms.cross_verification_note: The description details 'government financial assistance including grants, concessional loans, special tax benefits for R&D projects', which directly relates to public R&D funding.

reforms.description: Japan established R&D tax credits and accelerated depreciation allowances for research and development facilities to support technologically-advanced industries. Lower tax rates were also applied to income received from technology licensed overseas.
reforms.component_name: R&D Tax Credits and Depreciation Allowances
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: R&D tax credits and accelerated depreciation reduce the cost of R&D investment and incentivize private sector innovation and technology commercialization.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states 'established' without explicit date, but context suggests implementation during 1970s industrial policy period.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant innovation instrument reform providing multiple tax incentives for private R&D, but narrower in scope than comprehensive industrial policy.
reforms.source_quote: Government assistance to research and development in these various industries has been channelled through a number of grant programmes and a series of concessional loan programmes from the Japan Development Bank. Significant financial help was also provided through research and development tax credits, the accelerated depreciation of research and development facilities and lower tax rates on income received from technology licensed overseas.
reforms.cross_verification_note: The establishment of 'R&D tax credits and accelerated depreciation allowances for research and development facilities' supports innovation instruments for firms.

reforms.description: Japan established the Information Processing Association (IPA) in 1979 as a joint venture between government and the private sector to promote the development of highly sophisticated computer programmes, supported by the Japan Development Bank.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Public-private collaboration in software development supports technology transfer, knowledge sharing, and development of advanced computing capabilities.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant sectoral initiative establishing a new institutional mechanism for public-private collaboration in software development, but narrower than economy-wide reform.
reforms.source_quote: The Government has also directly participated in joint ventures with the private sector such as in 1979 with the setting up of the Information Processing Association (IPA) which aims at promoting the development of highly sophisticated computer programmes.
reforms.cross_verification_note: The creation of the Information Processing Association (IPA) to promote 'the development of highly sophisticated computer programmes' indicates a focus on knowledge transfer.

reforms.description: Japan implemented a four-year development plan (1979–1983) to develop very large-scale integrated circuitry (VLSI) for extra-high-capacity computers or 'fourth generation' computers, as part of MITI's computer industry development strategy, involving public-private collaboration.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Targeted R&D in advanced semiconductor technology supports innovation in computing and positions Japan competitively in high-technology sectors.
reforms.status_evidence: Text states 'implemented' a four-year plan beginning 1979.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant sectoral R&D initiative with multi-year commitment and public-private participation, but narrower than economy-wide industrial policy.
reforms.source_quote: Thus, three development plans were elaborated for the computer industry in 1972, 1976 and 1979. The latter covers a four-year project to develop by 1983 very large-scale integrated circuitry (VLSI) to be used in extra-high-capacity computers or 'fourth generation' computers.
reforms.cross_verification_note: The development plan for 'very large-scale integrated circuitry (VLSI)' is part of a strategy involving public-private collaboration in R&D, qualifying as sectoral R&D.

reforms.description: Japan established a development scheme for Light Water Reactor and Nuclear Generation in 1974 to support the nuclear energy machinery industry, providing government financial assistance for R&D in nuclear power plant technology.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Directed R&D in nuclear power technology supports energy security, industrial capability, and long-term technological advancement.
reforms.importance_rationale: Significant sectoral R&D initiative with government financial support, but narrower in scope than economy-wide industrial policy.
reforms.source_quote: A development scheme for Light Water Reactor and Nuclear Generation was also established in 1974 for the nuclear energy machinery industry.
reforms.cross_verification_note: The establishment of a development scheme for 'Light Water Reactor and Nuclear Generation' to support R&D in nuclear power plant technology aligns with sectoral R&D.
